nahhas-meani:1-2.t:
Among that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿حـمۤ عۤسۤقۤ﴾ [Verses 1, 2].
In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿حم. سق﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ʿAlī, peace be upon him, used to recognise the trials (fitan) by it.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿حـمۤ عۤسۤقۤ﴾: he said:
It is one of the names of the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُوحِيۤ إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾.
The meaning is: He reveals to you and to those before you, like the revelation
that preceded, or like the letters of the alphabet.
And it was said: no book was ever revealed without ﴿حم. عسق﴾ being in it.
So the meaning on this view is: like what has been revealed of this sura.
This is the position of al-Farrāʾ.
He said: and it is read ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُوحَى إلَيْكَ وَإلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ
قَبْلِكَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: On this reading it is possible that this is the end of the statement, and then He begins anew, saying: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾, on the basis that "al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm" is a khabar (predicate) or a naʿt (adjective), and the khabar is ﴿لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الأَرْضِ﴾.
And likewise on the reading of those who read ﴿نُوْحِي﴾ with nūn. And it is possible,
on the reading of those who read ﴿يُوْحَى﴾, that the meaning is: Allah reveals [it]; and
Sībawayh recited:
لِيُبْكَ يَزِيدُ ضَارِعٌ لِخُصُومَةٍ * وَأَشْعَثُ مِمَّنْ طَوَّحَتْهُ الطَّوَائِحُ
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [let him be wept for by] one humbled in a dispute, and a dishevelled one of those whom calamities have cast far away.)
So he said "let Yazīd be wept for", then made clear who ought to weep for him; so the meaning is:
one humbled weeps for him.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿تَكَادُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ يَنْفَطِرْنَ مِن فَوْقِهِنَّ﴾.
That is, they [almost] split apart from their tops, as a punishment.
Qatāda said: out of the majesty of Allah and His greatness.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And it was said: i.e. from above the nations that oppose [Him].
And it is read: ﴿يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْ فَوْقِهِنَّ﴾, i.e. from the greatness of the One who is above them.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
And in the earth are the believer and the disbeliever.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ of the believers.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is made clear by His saying, Majestic and Exalted, ﴿وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ
لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾, and He said about the disbelievers ﴿أُوْلَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللهِ، والمَلاَئِكَةِ، والنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لِّتُنذِرَ أُمَّ ٱلْقُرَىٰ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَتُنذِرَ يَوْمَ ٱلْجَمْعِ لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾.
Ashʿath narrated from al-Ḥasan, who said: ﴿أُمَّ ٱلْقُرَىٰ﴾ is Mecca.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It was called "the Mother of Towns" only because it was the first thing to be magnified
of the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; or because it was the first thing to be set down, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said
﴿إنَّ أوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ﴾.
And in the ḥadīth: "The earth was spread out from it."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: that you may warn the people of the Mother of Towns, and warn those around it.
﴿وَتُنذِرَ يَوْمَ ٱلْجَمْعِ﴾, that is, the day on which all people are resurrected.
The meaning is: and warn them of the Day of Resurrection; then the object and the bāʾ were omitted, as
the Exalted said ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ بَأْساً شَدِيداً مِنْ لَدُنْهُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَاطِرُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً وَمِنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ أَزْواجاً﴾.
﴿جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً﴾, that is, females; ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ أَزْواجاً يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ ﴾.
Mujāhid said: generation after generation, of people and of livestock.
Qatāda said: ﴿يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ﴾: He gives you life [and livelihood] in it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is that when He said ﴿جَعَلَ﴾ it indicated
the making (al-jaʿl) [to which the pronoun refers], just as it is said: "Whoever lies, it is evil for him" [i.e. the lying].
That is, He creates you and multiplies you in this making.
Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿فِيهِ﴾ means "bihi" (by it); and Allah knows best.
Al-Qutabī said: ﴿يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ﴾: in the spouse.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is as though the meaning according to him is: He creates you in the wombs of
the females, and ﴿فيه﴾ would be "in the womb"; but this is a mistake, because al-raḥim (the womb)
is feminine, and it has not been mentioned.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْبَصِيرُ﴾.
The kāf is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis; and Sībawayh recited:
"وَصَالِيَاتٍ كَكَمَا يُؤْثَفْينِ".
(And fire-blackened [hearthstones], like as they are set up as trivets.)

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَهُ مَقَالِيدُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقْدِرُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: al-maqālīd are the keys.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Whoever owns the keys owns the treasuries.
A key is called iqlīd, and its plural is irregular, like maḥāsin whose singular is ḥusn.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلدِّينِ مَا وَصَّىٰ بِهِ نُوحاً وَٱلَّذِيۤ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ﴾.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: That which He enjoined upon Noah «[Translator's note: the printed text has نواحاً, evidently a misprint for نوحاً]» is sincere devotion to Allah, and worshipping Him alone with no partner.
Mujāhid said: He enjoined upon Noah, and enjoined upon you, and enjoined upon all the prophets, one religion.
Al-Ḥakam said: Noah brought the law with the prohibition of mothers, daughters and sisters [in marriage].
Qatāda said: Noah brought the law with making lawful what is lawful and forbidding what is forbidden.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Abū al-ʿĀliya and Mujāhid is clear, because Islam
and sincere devotion are the religion of all the prophets, whereas the laws differ.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ أَنْ أَقِيمُواْ ٱلدِّينَ وَلاَ تَتَفَرَّقُواْ فِيهِ﴾.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَفَرَّقُواْ﴾, that is, do not be hostile to one another, and be brothers.
Qatāda said: So He informed that destruction lies in division, and that harmony lies in unity.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿كَبُرَ عَلَى ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مَا تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: They found it enormous, and the testimony "that there is no god but Allah
alone" weighed heavily upon them, and Iblīs and his troops were distressed by it; but Allah, Majestic and Mighty, refused anything but to give it victory,
make it prevail, and make it triumph over those who opposed it.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَجْتَبِيۤ إِلَيْهِ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِيۤ إِلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ﴾.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: He frees him from polytheism; and choosing (ijtibāʾ) is only from polytheism.
And Mujāhid said: ﴿يَجْتَبِي﴾: He makes pure.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَا تَفَرَّقُوۤاْ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ بَغْياً بَيْنَهُمْ﴾.
The meaning is: and they did not divide except on account of transgression, ﴿مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ﴾: the Qurʾān and the proofs of the truth of the prophethood of Muḥammad, peace be upon him.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى لَّقُضِيَ بِيْنَهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: they were deferred to the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَلِذَلِكَ فَٱدْعُ وَٱسْتَقِمْ كَمَآ أُمِرْتَ﴾.
It is placed later but intended to come earlier.
The meaning is: what you call the polytheists to is grievous for them; so to that call,
and be upright as you have been commanded.
﴿فَلِذَلِكَ﴾, that is, "fa-ilā dhālika" (so to that), i.e. to the establishment of the religion, as
the poet said:
 * "أَوْحَى لَهَا القَرَارَ فَاسْتَقَرَّتِ" *
(He inspired it [lahā] to be still, and it became still.)
That is, "awḥā ilayhā" (He inspired to it).

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآجُّونَ فِي ٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ مَا ٱسَتُجِيبَ لَهُ حُجَّتُهُمْ دَاحِضَةٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, after people had embraced Islam.
He said: And these are people who imagined that the Jāhiliyya would return.
Qatāda said: Those who disputed about Allah after He had been responded to are
the Jews and the Christians; they said: Our prophet came before your prophet, and our religion before your religion, and we are
better than you.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنزَلَ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ﴾.
Qatāda said: the Balance is justice.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَرِيبٌ﴾.
﴿لَعَلَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ﴾, that is, the resurrection is near «[Translator's note: hence the masculine قريب]».
Or: perhaps the coming of the Hour is near.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَسْتَعْجِلُ بِهَا ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهَا وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مُشْفِقُونَ مِنْهَا وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهَا ٱلْحَقُّ﴾.
That is, they say: When will it be? by way of denying it.
﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مُشْفِقُونَ مِنْهَا﴾, that is, afraid, because they are certain that it will happen.
﴿أَلاَ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُمَارُونَ فَي ٱلسَّاعَةِ﴾, that is, they dispute about it to make the believers doubt.
﴿لَفِي ضَلاَلٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾, because if they reflected, they would know that the One who
brought them into being and created them the first time is able to resurrect them.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ ٱلآخِرَةِ نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ﴾.
Al-ḥarth is work; and from it is the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar: "Till
for your world as though you will live forever, and work for your Hereafter as though you will die tomorrow." And from it
a man is named Ḥārith.
The meaning is: whoever by his work wants the Hereafter, ﴿نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ﴾,
that is, We grant him success and multiply good deeds for him.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ ٱلدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا﴾.
There are three views on its meaning:
a- Among them, that the meaning is: We give him of it what We will, as He, Glorified is He, said ﴿مَنْ كَانَ
يُرِيدُ العَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَاءُ لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ﴾.
b- And among them, that the meaning is: We ward off from him some of the afflictions of this world.
And the third view is that the meaning is: whoever does good in order to be praised, We leave him to that, and he has no share in the Hereafter.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿تَرَى ٱلظَّالِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا كَسَبُواْ وَهُوَ وَاقِعٌ بِهِمْ﴾.
That is, of the recompense of what they earned, which is the punishment, and it will befall them.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُل لاَّ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوَدَّةَ فِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾.
There are four views on its meaning:
1- Qazaʿa ibn Suwayd narrated from Abū Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Ibn
ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: Say: I do not ask you for any reward for what I have brought you, except
that you show love to Allah and draw near to Him through obedience to Him.
And Manṣūr and ʿAwf narrated from al-Ḥasan: ﴿قُل لاَّ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوَدَّةَ فِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾; he said: you show love to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and draw near
to Him through obedience to Him. This is one view.
2- Al-Shaʿbī, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: The meaning is: Say: I do not
ask you for any reward for it, except that you love me because of my kinship with you, and so protect me and do not deny me.
ʿIkrima said: Quraysh used to maintain their ties of kinship, but when the Prophet
ﷺ was sent, they cut him off; so he said: Maintain ties with me as you used to do.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on this view is: Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, but I remind you of my kinship — on the basis that it is an exception not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). These are two views.
3- Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: This verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by His saying, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿قُلْ مَا سَأَلْتُكُمْ مِنْ أَجْرٍ فَهُوَ لَكُمْ﴾. So what they had been asked was that they love him
for his kinship; then Allah brought him back to what the prophets were upon, as Noah and Hūd said
﴿قُلْ لاَ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيهِ أَجْراً﴾. These are three views.
4- Qays narrated from al-Aʿmash, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: When ﴿قُل لاَّ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوَدَّةَ فِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾ was revealed, they said: O Messenger of Allah, who are these whom we are to love?
He said: ʿAlī, Fāṭima and her children.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَن يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةً نَّزِدْ لَهُ فِيهَا حُسْناً﴾.
Iqtirāf is acquiring; it is taken from their saying "a man who is qarafa"
when he is a schemer.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً فَإِن يَشَإِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, if He wished, He would make you forget what He taught you.
And it was said: the meaning is: if He wished, He would take away your discernment, so thank Him since He has not done so.
And it was said: the meaning of ﴿فَإِن يَشَإِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ﴾ is: if Allah wished,
He would strengthen your heart with patience over their harm. And their saying ﴿ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾ completes the statement.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَيَمْحُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْبَاطِلَ وَيُحِقُّ ٱلْحَقَّ بِكَلِمَاتِهِ﴾.
That is, Allah erases polytheism and removes it.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقْبَلُ ٱلتَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَعْفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ﴾.
In the ḥadīth, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd was asked about a man who committed fornication with a woman: may he marry her? He said: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقْبَلُ ٱلتَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَعْفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَيَسْتَجِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ وَيَزِيدُهُم مِّن فَضْلِهِ﴾.
﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb), meaning: and He responds to those who
believe — as He, Glorified is He, said ﴿وَإِذَا كَالُوهُم﴾, i.e. "kālū lahum" (they measured for them). It is said:
"istajabtuhu" meaning "ajabtuhu" (I answered him); and al-Aṣmaʿī recited:
وَدَاعٍ دَعَا يَا مَنْ يُجِيبُ إلَى النَّدَى * فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِبْهُ عِنْدَ ذَاكَ مُجِيبُ
(Many a caller called: "O who will answer [the call] to generosity?" — and no answerer answered him then.)
And it is possible that it is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ), so that ﴿وَيَسْتَجِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ means: those who believe answer, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said
﴿فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Its literal sense is: let them seek the answer; this is
the literal meaning of [the form] "istafʿala".

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ بَسَطَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِعِبَادِهِ لَبَغَوْاْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلَـٰكِن يُنَزِّلُ بِقَدَرٍ مَّا يَشَآءُ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: The best provision is that which neither makes one transgress nor distracts.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ ٱلْغَيْثَ مِن بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُواْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُواْ﴾, that is, they had despaired.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said qanaṭa yaqniṭu, and qaniṭa yaqnaṭu, when one's despair of a thing
becomes intense.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ خَلْقُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَثَّ فِيهِمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: He meant "He spread in the earth" and not in the heaven, just as He,
Glorified is He, said ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ والمَرْجَانُ﴾, whereas they come only from the salt [water].
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake.
Warqāʾ narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying ﴿وَمَا بَثَّ فِيهِمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾: he said: people and angels.
And this is a good view; every living thing is called dābba, from dabba (to creep), so it is
dābb, and the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] is for intensification, as is said rāwiya and ʿallāma.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ جَمْعِهِمْ﴾, that is, to bring them back to life,
﴿إِذَا يَشَآءُ قَدِيرٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَآ أَصَابَكُمْ مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُواْ عَن كَثِيرٍ﴾.
It may be said: an affliction can occur for other than this reason; there are [several] answers to this:
a- Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿وَمَآ أَصَابَكُمْ مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾: he said: the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd).
So the meaning in this is: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made the ḥudūd on account of the sins
that are committed.
b- And it was said: ﴿ما﴾ here means "alladhī" (that which), and this is good.
The proof of this is that the people of Medina read ﴿بما﴾ without fāʾ.
So the meaning on this view is: and that which befell you was because of sins you committed.
c- Sufyān narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim, from al-Ḥasan, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
said: "There is no scratch from a stick, no stumble of a foot, and no
throbbing of a vein, except because of a sin; and what Allah pardons is more." Then
he recited ﴿وَمَآ أَصَابَكُمْ مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُواْ عَن كَثِيرٍ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So the meaning on this view is: whatever affliction befalls you that is
intended as punishment is because of what your hands have earned.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And there is a fourth view on the verse, namely: every affliction
that befalls is only on account of a sin: either a sin the person
has committed, or as a warning to him so that he does not commit it, or
as a trial for him so that his parents take heed. So on this view every affliction
is on account of sins, and the reading with the fāʾ becomes better, because it is
a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ ٱلْجَوَارِ فِي ٱلْبَحْرِ كَٱلأَعْلاَمِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: al-jawārī are the ships, and al-aʿlām are the mountains.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِن يَشَأْ يُسْكِنِ ٱلرِّيحَ فَيَظْلَلْنَ رَوَاكِدَ عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهِ﴾.
That is, motionless.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ بِمَا كَسَبُوا وَيَعْفُ عَن كَثِيرٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿يُوْبِقْهُنَّ﴾: He destroys them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said "awbaqathu dhunūbuhu", i.e. his sins destroyed him.
Qatāda said: ﴿أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ بِمَا كَسَبُوا﴾: He destroys those in them for their sins.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its implied structure is like ﴿واسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ وَٱلْفَوَاحِشَ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿كَبَائِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ﴾ is polytheism.
And it is read ﴿كَبِيرَ الإِثْمِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: The major sins are everything for which Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has promised the Fire.
And it was said: The major sins are everything for which Allah has promised the Fire and which
the Muslims agree is among the major sins. They have agreed that wine is among the major sins.
Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn
Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the saying of the Exalted
﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ وَٱلْفَوَاحِشَ﴾: "Associating partners [with Allah], despairing of the mercy of Allah, and feeling secure from the plan of Allah."
And among them are disobedience to parents, killing the soul that Allah has made sacred, slandering
chaste women, consuming the property of the orphan, fleeing from the battle-line, consuming
usury, sorcery, fornication, the false perjurious oath (al-yamīn al-ghamūs), embezzlement of spoils, withholding the obligatory zakat, false testimony, concealing
testimony, drinking wine, deliberately abandoning the prayer or anything
of what Allah has made obligatory, breaking the covenant, and severing the ties of kinship.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَأَمْرُهُمْ شُورَىٰ بَيْنَهُمْ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ﴾.
That is, they consult one another.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلْبَغْيُ هُمْ يَنتَصِرُونَ﴾.
Manṣūr narrated from Ibrāhīm: They used to dislike abasing
themselves, lest the wicked be emboldened against them.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَجَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِّثْلُهَا﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: If he says "May Allah disgrace him," the other says to him "May Allah disgrace him."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first is an evil deed in wording and meaning; the second
is an evil deed in wording, but in meaning it is not evil, nor is the one who does it
an evildoer. It was called an evil deed for the parallelism of the speech, so that it is known that it is a recompense
for the first.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَمَنِ ٱنتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مَا عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن سَبِيلٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: This is in retaliation (qiṣāṣ); as for one who wrongs you, it is not lawful
for you to wrong him.
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿وَلَمَنِ ٱنتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِ﴾: this is when his wrong is not
something that is improper.
That is, this is in what Allah has permitted retaliation for.
And Yūnus narrated from al-Ḥasan concerning His saying ﴿وَلَمَنِ ٱنتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِ﴾: he said: If he is cursed, he curses; and if he is reviled, he reviles — so long as it is not
a ḥadd (prescribed punishment) or a word that is improper.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَتَرَاهُمْ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا خَاشِعِينَ مِنَ ٱلذُّلِّ يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ﴾.
That is, they look at the Fire.
Mujāhid said: ﴿خَفِيٍّ﴾, that is, abased.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And it was said: they look with their hearts, because they are gathered blind.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِنَّ ٱلْخَاسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوۤاْ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
Qatāda said: They lost their families who are in Paradise, who had been prepared for them had they obeyed.
And it was said: since the believers will have their families joined to them in Paradise, and
the disbelievers will not be gathered with them in any good, they have lost them. Allah the Exalted said
﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَتُهُمْ بِإيمَانٍ أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مَا لَكُمْ مِّن مَّلْجَأٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِّن نَّكِيرٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿مِّن مَّلْجَأٍ﴾: of a stronghold; and ﴿مِّن نَّكِيرٍ﴾:
of a helper.
And it was said: ﴿مِّن مَّلْجَأٍ﴾: of an escape from the punishment of Allah.
﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ مِّن نَّكِيرٍ﴾, that is, you will not be able to deny the sins with which you are confronted.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَاثاً وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ٱلذُّكُورَ أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْرَاناً وَإِنَاثاً وَيَجْعَلُ مَن يَشَآءُ عَقِيماً﴾.
ʿAbīda, Abū Mālik, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said
— and the wording intended is that of ʿAbīda —: that is, He grants to whom He wills males who are born to him, and no females are born to him; and He grants to whom He wills females who are born to him, and no male is born to him; ﴿أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْرَاناً وَإِنَاثاً﴾: males are born to him and females are born to him.
ʿAbīda said: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُ مَن يَشَآءُ عَقِيماً﴾: no child is born to him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Any two things paired together are called "zawjān" (a pair), each one
of them being a "zawj" — among these are the man and the woman, the two leather socks and the two sandals. So the meaning of ﴿يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْرَاناً وَإِنَاثاً﴾ is: He pairs them, i.e. He pairs for them — as He said
﴿وَالقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾.
And it is said: "zawwajtu ibilī ṣaghīrahā wa-kabīrahā", i.e. I paired the young of my camels with the old.
And it is said: a man is ʿaqīm when no child is born to him, a woman is ʿaqīm when she does not give birth, and a wind is
ʿaqīm when it brings neither rain nor good.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ وَحْياً أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولاً فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾.
There are two views on the meaning:
a- That held by the people of tafsīr is what Mujāhid said; he said: ﴿إِلاَّ وَحْياً﴾:
that He breathes into his heart;
﴿أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ﴾: as He spoke to Moses, may Allah bless him
and grant him peace; ﴿أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولاً﴾: as He sent Gabriel, peace be upon him, to the Prophet
ﷺ and to those like him.
And the other view: that the meaning of ﴿إِلاَّ وَحْياً﴾ is as revelation was given to the prophets,
may Allah bless them, by sending Gabriel, may Allah bless him; ﴿أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ﴾:
as He spoke to Moses ﷺ; ﴿أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولاً﴾: to people in general.
And it is read ﴿أَوْ يُرْسِلُ رَسُولاً فَيوحِي بِإذْنِه﴾, and this is in the position of
a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. what takes the place of speech is what has been mentioned.
And it is possible that it is cut off from the first [i.e. a new sentence].

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ رُوحاً مِّنْ أَمْرِنَا﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: prophethood.
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is, and thus We have revealed to you that by which souls live, i.e. that by which they are guided.
Qatāda and al-Ḥasan said: ﴿رُوحاً مِّنْ أَمْرِنَا﴾, that is, a mercy from Us.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِيۤ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾.
That is, by what We have revealed to you.
Muʿallā said: I heard Ḥawshab read ﴿وَإنَّكَ لَتُهْدَى إلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾.
And in the reading of Ubayy: ﴿وَإنَّكَ لَتَدْعُو إلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is not to be recited, because it contradicts the written text of the muṣḥaf (al-sawād); rather,
anything like it is understood as coming from the one who said it by way of explanation, just as
Sufyān said concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِيۤ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾: i.e. "you call".
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِيۤ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾: he said: For every people there is a guide.
